arriving.title: Get a Virginia driver's license (REAL ID)
arriving.detail: New residents have 60 days. Bring ID, proof of your Social Security number, and two proofs of Virginia address (a lease counts as one). Book an appointment early.

arriving.title: 1. Get Virginia car insurance
arriving.detail: Get it before you register. Registering without insurance means a $600 fee and a suspended license.

arriving.title: 2. Safety inspection, plus emissions if your area requires it
arriving.detail: Northern Virginia localities require an emissions inspection.

arriving.title: 3. Title and register your car with the Virginia DMV
4. Register the car with your county or city
arriving.detail: Separate from the DMV, and it sets up personal property tax on the car. Arlington, for example, requires it within 30 days and a tax filing within 60.

arriving.title: Register to vote in Virginia
arriving.detail: Virginia also allows same-day registration with a provisional ballot after the regular deadline.

arriving.title: File a Virginia part-year resident return (Form 760PY)
arriving.detail: Plus a part-year return for the state you left, if it has income tax. Keep your lease or closing papers as proof of the dates.

arriving.title: Switch tax withholding to Virginia (Form VA-4)
arriving.detail: Give payroll a VA-4 and stop withholding for your old state as of your move date.

arriving.title: Update your health insurance
arriving.detail: Employer plan: update your address and check which local doctors are covered. Marketplace plan: moving lets you choose a plan through Virginia's Insurance Marketplace, usually within 60 days.
